title: Two LCLI-729 refusals name the wrong rule: a hand-qualified decision id in a repo with no origin, and a digits-only repository name
description:
Filed from the Stage 1 review of LCLI-729 (opum-ai/lore-cli#607, approved at c44fc400bfc4d36c4a8a5d996e76cd86ef2584af). Two non-blocking notes. BOTH are refusals that are CORRECT in outcome but name the WRONG rule; neither is a behaviour bug. Do NOT build this as part of #607 and do not expand #607.

N1 - A HAND-QUALIFIED ID IN A REPO WITH NO ORIGIN NAMES THE WRONG RULE. LCLI-729 gave qualifyDecisionRef a by-name refusal for a hand-supplied owner/repo qualifier ("the repository qualifier X is not a NAME"). But `lore link --decision opum-ai/lore-cli:DEC-9` in a bundle with NO readable origin and no `--repo` never reaches it: resolveDecisionQualifier (src/commands/link.ts:1172) runs FIRST and refuses with the generic `cannot qualify a decision id: this bundle has no readable origin remote`, plus the `--repo` hint. The input IS refused and nothing is written, so this is message quality rather than a hole — but the message names a rule the input did not break, and never says the qualifier is a PATH. Every test for the new refusal uses initRepoWithOrigin, so no test covers a repo with no origin. FIX: check the hand-supplied qualifier before requiring a qualifier at all (or resolve the qualifier lazily), so the by-name refusal wins. PROVE BOTH WAYS: with an origin the input is refused by name today, and without one it must be refused by the SAME name.

N2 - A DIGITS-ONLY REPOSITORY NAME IS REFUSED WITH NO EXPLANATION. LCLI-729 refuses a derived name that is numeric-only, because `https://host:8080` leaves the PORT as the last segment. The rule is right, but it ALSO catches a repository genuinely named in digits, e.g. github.com/org/2048. The user sees the same generic `no readable origin remote` with the `--repo` hint, so nothing says WHY the remote name was rejected. `--repo 2048` is the escape hatch and works. Untested, and NOT mentioned in the LCLI-729 CHANGELOG entry. FIX: name the reason in the refusal (the derived name, and that it is digits-only), add the test, and say it in the CHANGELOG. Also decide explicitly whether a digits-only name should be refused at all when the URL carries a real path segment — the port case is the LAST SEGMENT only because the path is empty, so the two are distinguishable.

N3 and N4 from the same review need no action and are recorded only so the review is not re-derived: CI="" or CI=false counts as set in the case-probe assertion test (harmless), and the Story (iii) arm calls loadProfile directly rather than through a CLI command (adequate for refused-at-load).

References: opum-ai/lore-cli#607, LCLI-729, src/core/decision-ref.ts, src/commands/link.ts.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A hand-supplied owner/repo qualifier in a bundle with no readable origin and no --repo is refused by the by-name qualifier rule, not the generic no-origin message.
A repository whose whole name is digits produces a refusal that names the derived name and says it is digits-only, with a test.
The CHANGELOG entry for that change names the digits-only refusal.
In test/agent-context-budgets.test.ts the anchored-case comment and its assertion agree: either the comment stops naming a count, or the test asserts the count the bare reference produces.

implementationNotes: N5 ADDED 2026-10-15, carried from the Stage 1 review of opum-ai/lore-cli#608 (LCLI-731 approval), at the leaders instruction. The test file comment in the new anchored-case arm says the anchored pack holds one section "not the four the bare reference produces below", but the bare-reference test asserts only `held.length` greater than 1 (about line 174), never 4. So the comment names a COUNT the suite does not pin, and the four is true of this fixture today rather than of anything asserted. FIX: either soften the comment to not name a number, or assert the count the bare reference actually produces so the two agree. It is a real, if small, overclaim in a comment - exactly the class LCLI-734 was filed to correct elsewhere in this suite, which is why it is worth carrying rather than dropping. NOT fixed on #608, which landed unchanged at 04b6c34d.
